title: Background Agent Partial Result Preservation

evaluation.reasoning: Automatic behavior requiring zero configuration. When a background agent is killed or interrupted, completed work is now preserved in conversation context instead of being lost. This is distinct from Autonomous Subagent Resume (v2.1.81, registry entry) — Resume is for cleanly stopped agents that the model decides to re-use; Partial Results is for forcibly killed agents where work is salvaged. Official Anthropic feature (releasebot tracks Claude Code releases). Integration complexity is 100 because there is no integration — it's behavior that already applies. Capability expansion is moderate (65) because the primary benefit is fault tolerance in long heartbeat runs, not a new workflow capability class. Token efficiency improves because less work is re-done on agent failure.
evaluation.action: Document in registry under Agent Orchestration section. Add playbook: helpers/playbooks/background-agent-partial-results.md with checkpoint recovery patterns for automation scripts. No configuration required.

original_description: When a background agent is killed or interrupted mid-task, its partial results are now preserved in the conversation context instead of being lost. Previously, killing a background agent discarded all in-progress work. Now, work completed before the kill is recoverable, enabling checkpoint-resume patterns. Complements the Autonomous Subagent Resume feature (v2.1.81) where the model decides to resume vs spawn fresh.
redundancy_check: NOVEL — registry has 'SendMessage Auto-Resume' and 'Autonomous Subagent Resume' but these are for resuming stopped agents. This is specifically about preserving partial output when an agent is killed (not stopped cleanly).
